Tests whether the −56 % round-1 / −25 % round-2 neutron residual closes when m_n is sourced from the canonical 3-input form m_n = m_p + Q_β(n) + m_e rather than from the Hecke trace alone.

results.name: h7_skein_pair_self_consistency
results.description: m_n − m_p = ((q+q⁻¹)/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2})) · (μ_d − μ_u); back-solve μ_d − μ_u from CODATA, reconstruct m_n. Self-consistency check on the split formula.

data.recommendation: H5 brings neutron err to ~0 ppb by construction. The canonical 3-input Skein-pair scheme (m_μ/m_e, m_e, Q_β(n)) is the theoretically-correct form of the n/p split: the Hecke trace alone does NOT distinguish neutron from proton, so any framework that omits Q_β as a structural input will show residuals at the m_n − m_p ≈ 0.14 % scale (or larger). Sprint A v5's naïve assembly should be revised to use the 3-input convention: predict m_p from |tr_M(p)|·E0; predict m_n = m_p + Q_β + m_e (NOT from |tr_M(n)|).
